blocks.text: 1. He Initialization
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445068787-810742120.png

Xavier Initialization's own genuine limitation with ReLU, covered as the previous topic's closing weakness, needed a direct, targeted fix. He Initialization makes one targeted mathematical adjustment specifically to address this exact issue.

It is named after its own original researcher, Kaiming He, and it is sometimes also called Kaiming Initialization for exactly this reason, both names referring to the exact same underlying technique covered fully throughout this topic.
2. Why Xavier Genuinely Struggles With ReLU

blocks.alt: Why Xavier Genuinely Struggles With ReLU
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445068788-822215658.png

This connects back to ReLU, already covered in its own dedicated topic. ReLU outputs exactly zero for roughly half of all typical inputs, a direct, well-established consequence of its own piecewise definition already covered in that earlier topic.

Xavier's own original derivation, already covered in the Xavier Initialization topic, assumed no such asymmetric zeroing behavior at all, and this mismatch causes activations to shrink more than Xavier's own formula actually expects, a genuine, real mathematical gap this topic directly addresses.
3. He's Formula

He Initialization uses a similar overall mathematical structure to Xavier's own formula, already covered in its own topic, but scales specifically based on only the number of inputs to a given layer, not inputs plus outputs combined.

This produces a genuinely larger scaling factor overall, directly compensating for ReLU's own roughly-half-zero output behavior already covered in the previous section, a deliberate, mathematically motivated adjustment rather than an arbitrary change.

blocks.text: 4. Compensating for Zeroed Neurons
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445068789-614298165.png

This connects back to ReLU's own exactly-zero output for negative inputs, already covered in its own dedicated topic. Roughly half the neurons in a typical ReLU layer output exactly zero, for any given input, a direct, structural consequence of ReLU's own definition.

He Initialization's genuinely larger scale, already covered in the previous section, keeps the remaining, active half's output well-behaved despite this zeroing, directly ensuring the overall layer's output variance still lands in a genuinely appropriate, well-scaled range.

blocks.title: info
blocks.content: This compensation is a genuinely elegant, direct mathematical response to a real, well-understood structural property of ReLU, rather than an empirical, trial-and-error adjustment discovered purely through experimentation.

blocks.text: 5. Becoming the Standard, Paired Default
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445068789-752615757.png

This connects back to ReLU's own status as today's actual default activation function, already covered in its own dedicated topic. He Initialization became the genuinely standard, paired default specifically for ReLU-based networks as a direct result.

The two are now almost always used together in real, modern practice, forming a genuinely well-matched, complementary pair, exactly like the sigmoid-and-Binary-Cross-Entropy pairing already covered in the Loss Functions module of this course.
6. Also Working Well for ReLU's Variants

This connects back to Leaky ReLU, PReLU, and ELU, all already covered fully in the Activation Functions module. He Initialization also genuinely works well for these ReLU variants too, not merely for plain ReLU alone.

This is since they all share ReLU's own broadly similar overall shape and behavior, already covered throughout their own respective topics, meaning the same underlying compensation He Initialization provides for plain ReLU's zeroing behavior remains genuinely appropriate for these closely related variants too.
7. The Genuine Modern Framework Default
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445068789-324710018.png

A genuinely important, practical fact worth knowing is that most modern Deep Learning frameworks now use He Initialization as their own actual default for many common layer types, particularly convolutional layers, covered in their own dedicated modules later in this course.

This directly reflects ReLU's own widespread, dominant use as today's standard activation function, already covered throughout the Activation Functions module, meaning the framework defaults themselves genuinely mirror the practical pairing already covered earlier in this topic.
8. Choosing Between Xavier and He
https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445068790-804293080.png

A genuinely simple, practical decision rule applies here. Using Tanh or Sigmoid calls for choosing Xavier Initialization, already covered fully in its own dedicated topic, matching its own original mathematical derivation.

Using ReLU or one of its own variants instead calls for choosing He Initialization, covered fully throughout this topic, exactly the targeted fix this entire topic was built specifically to provide for that particular family of activation functions.

blocks.text: 9. Recognizing When He Initialization Is Genuinely Right

blocks.alt: Recognizing When He Initialization Is Genuinely Right
blocks.text: https://algorithmxlr8-content-media.s3.ap-south-1.amazonaws.com/diagrams/1785445068790-477058875.png

Any hidden layer using ReLU or a ReLU variant, exactly today's actual, modern default already covered throughout much of the Activation Functions module, calls directly for He Initialization as its own genuinely matched, appropriate choice.

He Initialization is now, correspondingly, also the genuine, modern default choice across most real, practical Deep Learning training setups, a direct, natural consequence of ReLU's own overwhelming, widespread popularity already covered throughout this course.

blocks.text: 11. Weight Initialization: Module Recap

items: He Initialization makes a targeted mathematical adjustment to fix Xavier's own limitation with ReLU.
ReLU zeroes out roughly half of all typical inputs, a behavior Xavier's original derivation did not account for.
He Initialization scales based on only the number of inputs, producing a genuinely larger scaling factor.
This larger scale directly compensates for ReLU's structural zeroing, keeping the active half well-behaved.
He Initialization became the standard, paired default specifically for ReLU-based networks.
It also genuinely works well for Leaky ReLU, PReLU, and ELU, which share ReLU's broadly similar behavior.
Most modern frameworks now use it as their own actual default, reflecting ReLU's widespread, dominant use.
The simple rule: Tanh or Sigmoid calls for Xavier; ReLU or its variants call for He Initialization.
